My sorghum plot is 1.36 hectares here in the North West, and last year I put one bag of NPK 15-15-15 and topped with a little urea when the rains settled — I will do the same this year because the harvest was fair. I own this land, so I also carry manure from my goats and the small cattle my brother keeps, spreading it on the weaker patches before the first rains. I use my own sorghum seed saved from last harvest — the improved seed at the agro-dealer costs too much and my local variety does well enough when intercropped with cowpea. Pesticide I do not buy for sorghum, only sometimes a little for the cowpea if the pods are attacked; no irrigation here, we farm with the rains, and my two older sons help me weed so I only hire a few hands at planting and first weeding when the work is heavy.
